name: Lab Kiosk Navigation & Lockdown
description: Auto-hiding kiosk navigation bar and teacher lock curtain for Lab Kiosk OS.
_key_comment: Public key only. It fixes this extension's ID to hfjmbeplebjipenkfabncgkpadnjmmoe, which keeps the extension's storage and identity stable across rebuilds and is a prerequisite for ever force-installing it by id as a packed .crx. Note that the managed policy does NOT carry a blanket extension block: one would make Chromium refuse --load-extension and silently disable this extension. See the _extension_comment entries in etc/chromium/policies/managed/policies.json.
_permissions_comment: The agent's API is a different origin from whatever page the student is on, so the fetch lives in the service worker (which host_permissions covers) rather than in the content script (whose fetches are subject to the page's CORS). That is what lets the agent refuse wildcard CORS.
_storage_comment: chrome.storage.session holds the active broadcast epoch and URL. These used to live in the visited page's own sessionStorage, where that page's scripts could rewrite them to sit out a teacher's broadcast or re-enable Back at the broadcast root. Extension storage is in the extension's partition, so page script cannot reach it, and 'session' keeps the per-boot lifetime the kiosk wants.

content_scripts._all_frames_comment: true, so the keyboard and right-click lockdown also covers an embedded player or editor: key events inside an iframe never reach a listener in the parent document. The navigation bar and the lock curtain still build only in the top frame -- content.js returns early everywhere else.
